title: Entra Connect Health API flaw exposed tenant admin metadata
summary: Microsoft is notifying affected tenants through Azure Service Health that a vulnerability in the Entra Connect Health API, introduced on 23 July 2026 and found on 9 November, was exploited to read tenant-level metadata. According to the notification as reported by BleepingComputer, exposed data includes tenant technical-contact and admin email addresses, tenant ID, display and initial domain names, country/region, Entra licence tier, directory sync status and last sync time, Connect Health onboarding status and an expired, decommissioned agent registration certificate. Microsoft says it found read-only access and no configuration changes, deployed a server-side fix on 19 November and finished its investigation on 20 November; passwords, hashes, tokens, valid keys and on-premises topology were not exposed. Microsoft confirmed the fix and the notifications to BleepingComputer but has not said how many tenants were affected.
why: Admin and technical-contact addresses paired with tenant ID, licence tier and sync status are exactly what a targeted phishing or helpdesk social-engineering campaign against your privileged accounts needs. MSPs report notices for several customer tenants, arriving hours apart.
todo: Do now: check Azure Service Health (Security advisories) in every tenant you run, including customer tenants, for the Connect Health notice; absence in one tenant says nothing about the others.
Warn your service desk and the named admins/technical contacts about targeted phishing and fake support calls that quote tenant details.
Confirm every privileged role uses phishing-resistant MFA, and review Entra audit and sign-in logs for the admin accounts listed as contacts since late July.
Review Connect Health configuration and agent registrations; Microsoft's script at aka.ms/ConnectHealth/scripts shows current values only, not what was accessed.
No patch or customer remediation is required per Microsoft. Scope and attacker are not disclosed (not verified).
effective_note: Fixed server-side 19 Nov 2026; notifications from 20 Nov via Azure Service Health — per Microsoft as reported by BleepingComputer. The notice itself is not public.
